deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed from this page and p.36). pi^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,infinity}. It is generated by inertia loops l_0, l_1, l_inf with relation (12), essentially l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1 up to ordering convention. Gamma is the S_3 of permutations of {0,1,infinity}. It is lifted into an extension E of automorphisms of pi^ by elements tilde-rho (order 3, cyclic permutation) and tilde-sigma_i (involution fixing i and swapping the other two cusps). The previous page notes that the Klein 2-subgroups do not lift, because the local extensions do not split.

A candidate automorphism u~ = (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_inf), with p in Z^* (cyclotomic exponent), sigma in S_3 and g_i in pi^, sends l_i to int(g_i)(l_{sigma(i)}^p). Formulas (15) and (16) give conjugation by tilde-rho and tilde-sigma_0.

(a) Commuting with rho. u~ commutes with tilde-rho iff sigma lies in {1, rho, rho^2} and (17) holds: g_1 = rho(g_0), g_inf = rho^2(g_0). The first two equations already imply the third, g_0 = rho(g_inf), because rho^3 = id. So such u~ are parametrised by triples (p, sigma, g_0) in Z^* x A_3 x pi^. They are subject to (18): int(rho^2(g_0))(l_{sigma inf}^p) . int(rho(g_0))(l_{sigma 1}^p) . int(g_0)(l_{sigma 0}^p) = 1. This is the image of relation (12). One also needs the three factors to generate pi^, so that u~ is an automorphism.

(b) Commuting with sigma_0. The margin calls this 'moins intéressant pour la suite'. The condition is sigma in {1, sigma_0}, g_0 = sigma_0(g_0) and g_inf = sigma_0(g_1), hence g_1 = sigma_0(g_inf).

Grothendieck then corrects course. What really matters is the commutation of the hat-hat-Gamma, i.e. commutation modulo inner automorphisms (outer actions), not strict commutation.

In modern terms, this is a computation of the centraliser of the S_3-symmetry of P^1 - {0,1,inf} inside Aut(pi^_{0,3}) and Out. The single 'rho-symmetric' relation (18) is a non-normalised, symmetric form of the 3-cycle (hexagon) relation. Condition (b) plays the role of the 2-cycle relation. These are exactly the relations Ihara and Drinfeld (c.1989-91) used to define GT^, which contains G_Q via Belyi's theorem.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The bracketed '[?]' after 'g_0 = rho g_inf' in the transcription is just a word ('dans'/'déjà'), and the statement (cyclic consistency of (17)) is correct given rho^3 = 1 on pi^.
(18) as written is only the image-of-(12) condition. Generation of pi^ (that u~ is surjective) is noted separately and not addressed, as is usual.
Grothendieck himself flags that strict commutation is the wrong notion: one should work modulo inner automorphisms. So the parametrisation here is a preliminary step, not the final object.

ideas.what: Automorphisms of pi^_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}) described by data (p, sigma, g_0, g_1, g_inf): exponent p in Z^*, permutation of cusps, conjugators g_i, sending l_i to g_i l_{sigma i}^p g_i^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Braid-like / inertia-preserving automorphisms of F^_2; the (lambda, f) parametrisation of GT^
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981) treats Galois action on pi^_{0,3} with cusp-inertia data; Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower

ideas.what: Condition for commuting with the order-3 symmetry rho: g_1 = rho(g_0), g_inf = rho^2(g_0), giving the single relation (18)
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon) relation of GT^ in rho-symmetric normalisation
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche discussions of the S_3 action; not in this explicit form in published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Condition for commuting with the involution sigma_0: g_0 fixed by sigma_0, g_inf = sigma_0(g_1)
Recognition that the relevant notion is commutation modulo inner automorphisms (outer action, hat-hat-Gamma)
ideas.modern_name: Out(pi^) centraliser of S_3, i.e. outer GT-type action

missed.claim: In spring 1981 Grothendieck explicitly computed the centraliser of the S_3 symmetry of P^1-{0,1,inf} in the automorphisms of pi^. He obtained a cyclically symmetric hexagon-type relation (18) and the involution condition, i.e. a precursor of the defining relations of GT^ about 9 years before Drinfeld/Ihara. He then turned to the outer (mod-inner) version; this page is the last of the bundle, so that version is not carried out here.
missed.quote: Les u~ en question correspondent donc aux systèmes (p,sigma,g_0) ... tels que l'on ait ... (18) int(rho^2(g_0))(l_{sigma inf}^p). int(rho(g_0))(l_{sigma 1}^p). int(g_0)(l_{sigma 0}^p) = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents an early, symmetric (non-normalised) form of the GT relations in Grothendieck's own hand. It is relevant to the history of GT^ and to the Longue Marche to Esquisse transition. The rho-symmetric normalisation (conjugators rho^k(g_0)) differs from Drinfeld's f-normalisation and might be of interest for symmetric presentations of GT^.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an explicit 1981 hand computation of S_3-equivariant automorphisms of pi^_{0,3}, yielding hexagon- and 2-cycle-type relations, well before Drinfeld/Ihara's GT^. Grothendieck's anticipation of GT ideas is however broadly known (Longue Marche, Esquisse, Schneps' commentaries), and the page is preliminary: strict commutation, outer version not done.
transcription_corrections: '(rho, sigma, q_0) in Z^* x S_3^+ x pi^' should read '(p, sigma, g_0) in Z^* x S_3^+ x pi^': the first entry is the exponent p, not rho, and q_0 is g_0 throughout.
In (18) the superscripts are p, not rho: l_{sigma inf}^p, l_{sigma 1}^p, l_{sigma 0}^p. The arguments are rho^2(g_0), rho(g_0) and g_0.
First line: probably '(qui impliquent déjà g_0 = rho g_inf dans (17))'.
'il faut et [?] suffit' should read 'il faut et suffit'.
'sigma y commute à sigma_0' should read 'sigma commute à sigma_0'.
Last line: 'la commutation aux bouts intérieurs' is more plausibly 'la commutation mod automorphismes intérieurs'.
The circled reference before (18) is likely '(12)', the defining relation of pi^.
